title: Carbery–Wright oscillatory integral conjecture
statement:
Let $n,d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$ denote the polynomials in $n$ variables of degree at most $d$, and let $f\in\mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy

$$
\int_{[0,1]^n}f(x)\,dx=0,\qquad \int_{[0,1]^n}|f(x)|\,dx=1.
$$

**Carbery–Wright conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\left|\int_{[0,1]^n}e^{itf(x)}\,dx\right|\leq \frac{C\min\{d,n\}}{|t|^{1/d}}\quad\forall t\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}.
$$

This conjecture is an oscillatory-integral formulation motivated by sharp polynomial sublevel-set estimates on convex bodies. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02679

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2025). “This long-standing problem was resolved only recently by B. Klartag and J. Lehec .”
source_name: Egor Kosov, “Oscillatory integrals with polynomial phase and regularity of distributions”, arXiv:2511.02679 (2025).
